It's a three way tie between adventure, fighting, and action RPGs. Strange combination? The gist of it is that I like a great story, and yet I want a game to be a game, filled with action and excitement. 90s era JRPGs were amazing in an era when nobody else was that nuanced about storytelling, but fast forward to the present, RPG mechanics have largely stagnated, whereas just about every game on the market now has a plot and a story to tell. The mechanics of Final Fantasy and Persona games have long felt stale so I prefer more of an action element, and while JRPGs can be enjoyable, I also don't like clumsy mechanics or a need for excessive grinding. As for the fighting game part, in between great stories I like a challenge that stays fresh but permits me to build upon the things I've learned about common gameplay mechanics (i.e. 2D fighting games share a lot of iconic characteristics even across companies, so experience from past fighting games feeds into newer ones well).

I also like puzzles that tell a story:

  • Ico

  • Catherine

And I have a soft spot for point and click adventure games:

  • Broken Age

  • Monkey Island

  • Grim Fandango
